judged_by: Matched by a Claude Opus 5.5 agent on 2026-11-25; not yet checked by the labeler.

question.note: How attitudes and behaviour may have shifted from initial doses to boosters: accurate to p.7, not a gold question (the p.7 'may have' hedge is lost but it is framed as a question).
The non-significant vaccination interaction and the mandates explanation (F4), placed in the question slot.

central_claim.note: Conservative half of C1 (less hesitant and more boosted in liberal regions); the liberals-regardless half is only in a quote, not in the claim.

evidence.note: Online survey of 683 US participants in early 2023: the data source, without the nonprobability convenience sample or Qualtrics Panels recruitment. N = 683 without the screening numbers (E2). The demographic controls are a fragment of E6.
Hesitancy half of E5 (seven modified AAVS items); booster hesitancy items from a 2022 survey also accurate. Status half in [5].
Says quotas for race, income and gender (gender cap is on p.4) but not the four Black/White by above/below-median groups or why; the quotes carry the detail.
Self-reported vaccine and booster status (the other half of E5).
OLS for hesitancy, logit GLMs for status; no interaction term here.
Linear models with the interaction for hesitancy (Table 4 caption).
Logistic models with the interaction for status (Table 6 caption).

key_findings.note: Hesitancy interaction significant, without its shape.
Liberals-regardless half of F2; the steeper rise in conservative climates is not stated in this slot, so F2 is not joined.
Conservative half of F3 (60% vs under 35%); liberals boosted anywhere is missing. 'Varied significantly' is fair since the booster interaction was significant.
'Did not significantly affect' is loose wording for a non-significant interaction; not flagged.
No differences by race or gender in hesitancy or status: accurate to p.5 (Table 2), not in the gold.

scope_and_limits.note: Zip-code data may miss other regional variables such as population density that could drive the results: proxy plus consequence.
Effect modification not tested, without the consequence; the consequence is in [6].
Simpson's paradox / pooled associations as averages: the consequence half of L5.

theoretical_positioning.note: Prior work treated orientation and climate separately; this study tests their interaction. Same call as the earlier judge on like wording (no 'first' needed).

interlocutor_claim.note: Prior studies treated orientation or climate separately, not their interaction; the paper's building on them is implied by 'rather than how they interact'.
